title: Clamp two precast gels into an SDS-PAGE electrode assembly
instruction: Clamp both gels into the electrode assembly, ready to run. Finish with both arms back where they started.
context: SDS-PAGE is how protein, molecular-biology and clinical research labs separate proteins by size, several times a week at a typical bench, and the Bio-Rad Mini-PROTEAN Tetra is one of the most used mini-gel cells. Every run starts by clamping two precast gel cassettes into the cell's electrode assembly. The maker's manual has one hand squeeze both cassettes flat against the green gaskets while the other slides the clamping arms over them; a cassette that shifts during the lock leaks buffer and the run is lost. This trial is that dry assembly step.
setup: A lab bench in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances: forward from the line between the arm bases, sideways from the midpoint between them; heights above the bench top. (1) Bench top: black epoxy resin, 1 cm thick, 15 to 52 cm forward, 27 cm right to 27 cm left, fixed. (2) A Bio-Rad Mini-PROTEAN Tetra electrode assembly (cat. 165-8037; the one in the 2-gel cell 1658005), standing 30 cm forward on the centre line, its long side across, fixed in place (in a real trial, by two strips of double-sided foam tape under its base). Glass-filled PBT frame: base 7.2 x 12.8 cm, 0.6 cm thick; core 2.5 cm thick and 9.9 cm wide with an open inner chamber, end posts 10.4 cm tall, banana plugs on top (red anode at the right-hand end, black cathode at the left) to 12 cm. On each face a green silicone U gasket 1.5 mm proud, its legs 0.8 cm wide with a notch at the top of each, 9.05 cm up. Two gel supports per side, 6 cm apart: seats 1.4 cm up sloping 12 degrees down outward, a 2 mm lip, and back rests that hold a resting cassette at 30 degrees. Two green clamping arms (C-shaped clamps 4.8 cm wide, 9.4 cm tall, 30 g), each on a pivot 1 cm up at its end of the frame, 5.4 cm from the centre line, swung out 35 degrees (the open position). (3) Two Bio-Rad Mini-PROTEAN TGX precast gel cassettes (10%, 10-well, cat. 4561034): 10 cm wide, 8.5 cm tall (the short plate 7.5 cm), 5.5 mm thick, styrene copolymer plates with the 1 mm gel sealed between, 40 g each; comb and green tape already removed, wells rinsed and drained, outside wiped dry. Each rests on the two supports of one side, short plate facing the gasket, its bottom on the seats, leaning 30 degrees out against the back rests: one toward the robot, one away. The trial starts after the manual's step 1b: precast cassettes come flat in their pouches, so the person resetting the trial sets them on the supports. (4) Scenery, fixed: the Mini-PROTEAN Tetra mini tank (clear polycarbonate, 12 x 16 cm, 15 cm tall) 44.5 cm forward, 16.5 cm right; its lid upside down, red and black leads up, 44.5 cm forward, 17.5 cm left; the opened gel box (white card, 12 x 15 x 3.5 cm) 21.5 cm forward, 20.5 cm left. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot. No buffer, water or power is used: the trial is the dry assembly.
scoring: Each clamping arm turns on its pivot from 35 degrees open to 0 (shut). Its walls close over both cassettes' side edges only while both cassettes lie within 3 mm of the gaskets at its end; otherwise it stops 20 degrees short against the leaning cassette's edge. Closing takes 0.45 N m (5 N at its thumb tab) until, within 6 degrees of shut, it passes over centre and locks; a locked arm takes 0.45 N m to pull open. A cassette let go of falls back to its 30-degree lean. A cassette is seated when its short plate lies flat on the gasket (within 1 mm at the bottom and at the short plate's top, at both ends), facing the right way, with the short plate's top 0-3 mm below the gasket's notch. Judged at the end of the trial on live states: 1.0: both arms locked, both cassettes seated and both robot arms back where they started (each fingertip centre within 5 cm of its start); 0.75: both arms locked and both cassettes seated; 0.5: one arm locked with both cassettes seated; 0.25: both cassettes lay flat on their gaskets at the same moment at some point in the trial; else 0.0. A cassette that falls onto the bench scores 0.0 for the trial. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held 1 s with both cassettes and both clamping arms still. In a real trial: an arm is locked when it stands upright against its end of the frame, snapped over centre (photo); a cassette is seated when, looking down at each notch, the top of its short plate touches the green gasket just under the notch (the maker's leak checks) and a 1 mm feeler gauge does not enter between short plate and gasket at either notch; the 0.25 tier and falls are judged from the video; the robot arms against marks at their start.
reset_notes: Swing both clamping arms open (35 degrees out), lift the two cassettes out and stand them back on their gel supports with the short plates facing the gaskets, leaning out against the back rests; check the electrode assembly stands on its marks.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim, PhysX, 20 Hz) at real size; the electrode assembly is fixed in place and its gaskets are rigid. Each clamping arm is a revolute joint with a spring capped at 0.45 N m and an over-centre lock. A rule stands in for its walls meeting a leaning cassette's edge: it stops 20 degrees short unless both cassettes lie within 3 mm of the gaskets. The arms' cassette-lifting pins are not modelled. Cameras 1280x704 (Dream-1: 320x176).
